cases.input: Compare two biosensor technology offers for the same IVD workflow using a common requirement set, vendor specifications, pilot data, integration constraints and dated commercial assumptions.
requiredBehaviors: compare both offers against identical decision criteria and explicit requirements
separate vendor claims from confirmed evidence using evidence origin type independence and confidence
make commercial assumptions quantity and time specific and route IP regulatory and supplier questions
forbiddenBehaviors: reward one offer for providing more marketing detail by silently changing the comparison criteria
infer FTO or regulatory approval from the offer documents

cases.input: A vendor claims exceptional analytical sensitivity and production readiness but provides only marketing graphics, selected prototype results and no independent replication or manufacturing-capability evidence.
requiredBehaviors: keep the sensitivity and maturity claims visible but lower confidence based on evidence origin type and independence
mark unverified production readiness and scale capability as unknown or conditional
capture missing sample size comparator replication and transferability evidence where relevant
forbiddenBehaviors: convert marketing claims into confirmed performance facts
assign production readiness from brochure language alone

cases.input: A draft offer analysis concludes that the platform is ready for the target workflow solely from a pitch deck and an attractive price quote, while regulatory and IP questions remain unassessed.
requiredBehaviors: reject the combined conclusion as unsupported
separate technical maturity regulatory assessment and IP FTO into their proper evidence and routing paths
forbiddenBehaviors: treat price attractiveness as evidence of technical or regulatory suitability

cases.input: Vendor A supplies one hundred pages of polished marketing and specifications with no independent replication. Vendor B supplies ten pages containing a small independent validation study with raw-data access. Both are assessed against the same requirements.
requiredBehaviors: keep the comparison criteria identical for both vendors
distinguish evidence volume from evidence quality and independence
give the independent validation stronger evidentiary weight where otherwise comparable
forbiddenBehaviors: reward Vendor A simply because it supplied more pages
treat specifications and independent validation as equivalent evidence types

cases.input: Vendor A has clearly stronger technical performance for the target assay but requires an uneconomic minimum volume, high switching cost and expensive proprietary consumables.
requiredBehaviors: rate technical fit independently from commercial feasibility and vendor dependency
allow strong technical fit to coexist with weak or conditional commercial fit
surface switching burden without making the overall strategic-fit decision
forbiddenBehaviors: downgrade technical performance merely because the offer is expensive
collapse technical and commercial dimensions into a single score
make a strategic-fit conclusion that belongs to the due-diligence orchestrator
skillAnchors: Technischer Fit und Commercial Feasibility bleiben getrennte Dimensionen
Strategic fit gehört nicht in diesen Skill
